humanities_role_explanation: The benchmark targets competence in cultural heritage knowledge itself: questions span a heritage framework (types, values, conservation, management, utilization) and responses are judged against scholarly consensus by heritage professionals. Heritage is the subject of inquiry, not just raw text.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Single-turn text queries and text responses from LLMs; multimodal use is explicitly listed as unexplored.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Queries come in four types: critical query (open-ended opinion/discussion), fact verification (including True/False), causal inference (inferring from archaeological evidence), and interpretation (explaining terms, events, objects). LLM responses are classified into eight value-misalignment types (detail inaccuracy, cultural misunderstanding, knowledge gap, premature certainty, cultural reductionism, historical bias, selective narration, contextual irrelevance), which involves normative and cultural judgment about generated texts.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single domain (cultural heritage) and a single phenomenon (value misalignment).

evaluates_generative_llm.note: LLaMA-3-8B, Qwen-7B, Baichuan2-7B, Yi-6B, Mistral-7B; GPT-4o used for task generation and as judge.

quantitative_metrics.note: Value misalignment rates per aspect, type and model; Likert severity scores.

summary: The paper introduces CHVM-1K, 1066 cultural-heritage queries organized in a 5-category, 17-aspect framework, and evaluates five open-source LLMs for cultural value misalignment. Responses are labeled by GPT-4o with in-context examples plus 17 heritage professionals, yielding eight misalignment types and rates over 65%.
key_findings: Over 65% of generated texts show notable misalignment; per-aspect total rates range from 30.16% (A3, Yi-6B) to 92.42% (A6, LLaMA-3-8B). Contextual irrelevance (VM8) and detail inaccuracy (VM1) are the most frequent types, and premature certainty (VM4) the least. LLaMA-3-8B is worst, Mistral-7B slightly best. Professionals rated VM1 most severe.
facets_explanation: Questions were generated by ChatGPT from professional-selected keywords and refined by heritage professionals. Misalignment labels came from GPT-4o with in-context examples, then 17 heritage professionals in a two-round process, with disagreements resolved by group consensus (treated as noise). Judging responses requires scholarly knowledge not in the query, and no per-community gold answers are used.
results_explanation: The 92.42 figure is the highest total misalignment rate (A6, LLaMA-3-8B), i.e. the worst result, since no best-model headline is reported; the metric is misalignment rate, not accuracy. The text states the rate ranges 'from 30.16% for tasks within A3 on the Yi-6B model to 92.42%' and that 'over 65%' of texts are misaligned. Asymmetry is flagged in the limitations: the dataset mainly covers Asian heritage and underrepresents Africa, Latin America and indigenous communities.
